glance_notes.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — 2026 Mississippi Voter Information Guide
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: To vote in Mississippi's November 3, 2026 General Election, eligible residents must register by October 5, 2026. Mail-in voter registration applications must be postmarked by that date.

glance_notes.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Absentee Voting Information
glance_notes.text: No General No-Excuse Early Voting: Mississippi does not provide general no-excuse early voting. Voters who meet an absentee-voting qualification may vote absentee in person at their Circuit Clerk's Office beginning September 19, 2026. The deadline for in-person absentee voting for the November General Election is October 31.

glance_notes.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Voter ID
glance_notes.text: Photo ID Required: Mississippi generally requires an accepted photo ID for in-person voting, including in-person absentee voting. A voter who does not have acceptable photo identification on Election Day may cast an affidavit ballot and then has five business days to present acceptable identification or apply for a free Mississippi Voter ID Card.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Mississippi residents may register in person at a Circuit Clerk's Office, Municipal Clerk's Office, through the Department of Public Safety when obtaining a driver's license, through certain government agencies, or by submitting a mail-in voter registration application. Mississippi does not provide general online voter registration for new voters. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be a resident of Mississippi and the applicable county, city or town for at least 30 days, be at least 18 years old by the applicable election, not have been declared mentally incompetent by a court, and not be disqualified by a Mississippi conviction for a disenfranchising crime unless voting rights have been restored as provided by law.
register.glance_value: Register in person or by mail
register.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — How Do I Register to Vote?
register.internal_note: Mississippi does not currently provide general online registration for new voters. Y'all Vote provides online registration verification and an online update service for already-registered Mississippi voters who have a valid Mississippi driver's license or DPS-issued photo ID. Mississippi's felony disenfranchisement rules apply to a specific list of crimes rather than every felony. The Secretary of State's current list is available at [https://www.sos.ms.gov/content/documents/elections/2025%20Disenfranchising%20Crimes.pdf](https://www.sos.ms.gov/content/documents/elections/2025%20Disenfranchising%20Crimes.pdf).

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Mississippi Secretary of State's Y'all Vote voter information hub to verify your voter registration. Registered voters can also use the state's online services to update registration information when eligible. If information is incorrect or you need assistance, contact your county Circuit Clerk.
check_registration.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Y'all Vote
check_registration.internal_note: Y'all Vote directly provides Voter Registration Verification, registration cancellation and registration-update services. The online update function requires the voter to already be registered in Mississippi and have a valid Mississippi driver's license or DPS-issued photo ID.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: To vote in Mississippi's November 3, 2026 General Election, eligible residents must register by October 5, 2026. A mail-in voter registration application must be postmarked by October 5. Mississippi generally requires registration at least 30 days before an election and does not provide general Election Day voter registration.
deadlines.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — 2026 Mississippi Voter Information Guide
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 Voter Information Guide directly states that voters must register by October 5 for the November 3 General Election. Mississippi's registration materials establish the underlying 30-day rule. The official mail-in registration form states that an application must be postmarked or hand-delivered to the Circuit Clerk's Office no later than 30 days before the election.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use the Mississippi Secretary of State's My Election Day service through Y'all Vote to locate your polling place. The service also provides personalized sample-ballot information and other election information. A voter's registration card identifies the precinct and polling location associated with the registration. Because polling locations can change, voters should verify their location before Election Day or contact their Circuit Clerk.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your polling place with My Election Day
polling_place.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Y'all Vote
polling_place.internal_note: The current Y'all Vote page states that My Election Day locates polling places and provides sample ballots. The 2026 Voter Information Guide states that the voter registration card provides the name, location and number of the voter's precinct.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Mississippi's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polls are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. Voters who are in line at 7:00 p.m. have the right to vote. Mississippi generally requires voters to present an accepted photo ID when voting in person. A voter without acceptable photo identification may cast an affidavit ballot and has five business days after Election Day to present acceptable identification or apply for a free Mississippi Voter ID Card.
election_day.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — 2026 Mississippi Voter Information Guide
election_day.internal_note: The official 2026 Voter Information Guide directly states that polls are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. The current County Election Handbook confirms the right to cast a ballot when in line at 7:00 p.m. The Secretary of State Voter ID page establishes the affidavit-ballot procedure for voters without acceptable photo identification.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Mississippi polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who is in line by 7:00 p.m. is allowed to remain and cast a ballot.
polling_hours.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — 2026 Mississippi Voter Information Guide
polling_hours.internal_note: The Secretary of State's 2026 Voter Information Guide directly establishes 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. Election Day polling hours. The current County Election Handbook at [https://www.sos.ms.gov/content/documents/Elections/County%20Election%20Handbook.revised%209.18.2023.pdf](https://www.sos.ms.gov/content/documents/Elections/County%20Election%20Handbook.revised%209.18.2023.pdf) confirms that voters in line at 7:00 p.m. have the right to vote.

early_voting.label: In-Person Absentee Voting
early_voting.content: Mississippi does not provide general no-excuse early voting. Voters who qualify to vote absentee may vote absentee in person at their Circuit Clerk's Office. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, in-person absentee voting begins September 19 and continues through October 31. Circuit Clerk's Offices provide in-person absentee voting from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday and are also scheduled to be open from 8:00 a.m. until noon on Saturday, October 24 and Saturday, October 31. Eligibility requirements apply.
early_voting.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Absentee Voting Information
early_voting.internal_note: Mississippi should not be described as having ordinary no-excuse early voting. The Secretary of State's current 2026 absentee page directly establishes September 19-October 31, Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., plus October 24 and October 31 from 8:00 a.m.-noon. Only voters meeting an absentee qualification may use this process.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Mississippi generally requires a voter to qualify under one of the absentee-voting reasons established by state law. Voters should contact their county Circuit Clerk to determine eligibility and request a ballot. Mail-in absentee ballots for the November 3, 2026 General Election are available no later than September 19. Completed mail-in absentee ballots must be postmarked on or before November 3 and received by the Circuit Clerk on or within five business days after the election. For the 2026 General Election, the final receipt date is November 10. Mississippi requires absentee ballot envelopes to be properly witnessed as provided by law.
absentee_mail.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Absentee Voting Information
absentee_mail.internal_note: The Secretary of State's live 2026 absentee guide directly establishes September 19 availability, an Election Day postmark deadline and November 10 receipt deadline. It also explains Mississippi's witness requirement. In general, the absentee ballot envelope must be witnessed by an official authorized to administer oaths, such as a notary public. A voter who is temporarily or permanently physically disabled may instead use a witness who is at least 18 years old. Eligibility varies by statutory category, so the reader-facing text directs voters to their Circuit Clerk rather than presenting an incomplete list.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Mississippi generally requires voters to show an accepted photo ID when voting in person, including when voting absentee in person at a Circuit Clerk's Office. Accepted identification includes a valid Mississippi driver's license, Mississippi state-issued identification card, U.S. passport, qualifying government employee photo ID, Mississippi license to carry a pistol or revolver containing a photo, tribal photo ID, U.S. military photo ID, or current valid student photo ID issued by an accredited Mississippi college, university, community college or junior college. Certain voters with religious objections to being photographed and certain residents of state-licensed care facilities are exempt. A voter without acceptable photo ID on Election Day may cast an affidavit ballot and has five business days to present acceptable identification or apply for a free Mississippi Voter ID Card.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID required; affidavit ballot available
voter_id.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Voter ID
voter_id.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current Voter ID page directly lists accepted identification, exemptions and the five-business-day affidavit-ballot cure procedure. Free Mississippi Voter ID Cards are available to eligible voters without another acceptable form of photo identification through Circuit Clerk offices.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Mississippi provides accessible voting machines at polling places for voters with disabilities. A voter who is blind, physically disabled or unable to read or write may request assistance with marking a ballot. The voter may select a person to provide assistance, subject to restrictions established by law, or receive assistance through the polling-place process. Voters with temporary or permanent physical disabilities may also qualify for absentee voting and have special witness provisions when returning a mail-in absentee ballot.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible machines, assistance and absentee options
accessible_voting.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Voter Registration Information
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current NVRA guidance states that accessible voting machines for voters with disabilities are located in every Mississippi polling place and explains assistance rights. Under Mississippi law, assistance may be requested by a voter who is blind, physically disabled or unable to read or write. Certain people are prohibited from providing assistance, including a candidate on the ballot, specified relatives of a candidate, poll watchers, the voter's employer or employer's agent, and officers or agents of the voter's union.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Mississippi provides special absentee-voting procedures for eligible military members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas under the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot, and the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available as a backup when applicable. Mississippi provides electronic transmission of voter registration and absentee-ballot materials to military and overseas voters and operates SafeVoteMS for eligible UOCAVA voters. Because military and overseas procedures and deadlines differ from ordinary domestic absentee voting, covered voters should use Mississippi's official UOCAVA resources or contact their Circuit Clerk.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, FWAB and electronic UOCAVA services available
military_overseas.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Military & Overseas Voter Information
military_overseas.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current military and overseas page provides FPCA, FWAB, fax and return-envelope resources and SafeVoteMS for UOCAVA voters. It also states that Mississippi provides electronic transmission of voter-registration and absentee-balloting materials. Do not apply the ordinary domestic absentee rules to UOCAVA voters without checking the specific federal and Mississippi procedures.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: Mississippi college students must register at the place they consider their permanent residence. A student may keep a qualifying permanent residence at a parent's or guardian's home or may register at a campus dormitory or apartment if the student considers that school residence to be the permanent residence. A voter may legally be registered in only one county. Students who will be away from the county where they are registered when an election occurs should contact that county's Circuit Clerk to determine whether they qualify to vote absentee.
student_voting.glance_value: Choose one qualifying home or school residence
student_voting.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Voting as a College Student
student_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State's dedicated college-student page expressly presents two residence choices: the parent's or guardian's home or the student's campus dormitory/apartment, depending on which the student considers the permanent residence. It also emphasizes that the voter may legally be registered in only one county and directs students who will be away to discuss absentee eligibility with their Circuit Clerk.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Mississippi voters can use the Secretary of State's My Election Day service through Y'all Vote to view personalized sample-ballot information. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's residential address, precinct and electoral districts, voters should use their own address to review the ballot information that applies to them. Voters also have the right to review a sample ballot posted at the polling place before voting.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your ballot with My Election Day
sample_ballot.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State — Y'all Vote
sample_ballot.internal_note: The current Y'all Vote page directly states that My Election Day provides sample ballots tailored to the voter. The current County Election Handbook also establishes the right to review the sample ballot posted at the polling place before voting. General Election ballot information should be reverified closer to November as ballot preparation is finalized.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Mississippi Secretary of State Elections & Voting website and Y'all Vote for official statewide voter information. Y'all Vote provides voter registration verification, registration resources, polling-place information, personalized sample ballots, absentee and affidavit ballot tracking, voter ID information and election resources. County Circuit Clerks administer voter registration, absentee voting and many local election functions.
